group.title: Films, music and free time
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A live performance of pop or rock music.
examples: The band is playing a {gig} at the club tonight.
wrong: We went to a gig and listened to a silent library.

words.meaning: An exciting book or film, often about crime or danger.
examples: I couldn’t put down the {thriller} until the last page.
wrong: The thriller was so boring and calm that I fell asleep.

words.meaning: A type of film or story that is meant to frighten people.
examples: I never watch {horror} films alone at night.
wrong: We watched a horror movie to feel calm and relaxed.

words.meaning: Words at the bottom of the screen that translate what people say.
examples: We watched the French film with English {subtitles}.
wrong: The subtitles were the music played at the start of the film.

words.meaning: The place at a theater or cinema where tickets are sold.
examples: We bought our tickets at the {box office}.
wrong: The box office is where actors change their clothes.

words.meaning: One part of a TV or radio series.
examples: I watched the first {episode} last night.
wrong: An episode is the whole series from start to end.

words.meaning: To practice a play, piece of music or show before performing it.
examples: The actors {rehearsed} for weeks before the opening night.
wrong: They rehearsed the show after the last performance had finished.

words.meaning: A short break between the parts of a play or concert.
examples: We bought drinks during the {intermission}.
wrong: The intermission is the main part of the show.

words.meaning: The hobby of making clothes from wool with two long needles.
examples: My grandmother loves {knitting} scarves for the family.
wrong: He took up knitting and made a cake.

words.meaning: The art or hobby of taking photos.
examples: She studied {photography} and now works for a magazine.
wrong: His hobby is photography, so he has never used a camera.

words.meaning: A large park with rides and shows built around one subject.
examples: The kids loved the rides at the {theme park}.
wrong: A theme park is a quiet place to read books.

words.meaning: A ride at a fair with small cars that go very fast up and down steep tracks.
examples: The {roller coaster} went upside down twice.
wrong: The roller coaster moved so slowly that the children fell asleep.

words.meaning: A famous person’s name written by them for a fan.
examples: She asked the singer for his {autograph}.
wrong: The fan gave her own autograph to the star to remember her.

words.meaning: To keep people interested and amused.
examples: The clown {entertained} the children for an hour.
wrong: The comedian entertained the crowd by boring them to sleep.

words.meaning: Fun and enjoyable to watch, read or listen to.
examples: It was a very {entertaining} show.
wrong: The play was so entertaining that everyone left early.

words.meaning: Extremely funny.
examples: The new comedy is {hilarious}.
wrong: The joke was hilarious, so no one laughed.

words.meaning: So exciting that it holds your attention completely.
examples: It’s a {gripping} story with a surprise ending.
wrong: The gripping film was so dull that I left after ten minutes.

words.meaning: The part of a song that is repeated after each verse.
examples: Everyone sang along to the {chorus}.
wrong: The chorus is the part of the song that is sung only once.

words.meaning: A series of musical notes that make a song you can hum.
examples: She hummed a happy {tune} as she worked.
wrong: The tune was just the words of the song with no music.

words.meaning: A list of songs chosen to be played in order.
examples: I made a {playlist} for our road trip.
wrong: A playlist is the stage where the band plays.

words.meaning: Singing popular songs to recorded music while reading the words on a screen.
examples: We sang {karaoke} at the party until midnight.
wrong: At karaoke, everyone stays silent and listens to the radio.

words.meaning: A word puzzle where you write answers into a grid of small squares.
examples: He does the {crossword} in the newspaper every morning.
wrong: She finished the crossword by drawing a picture of a cat.

words.meaning: Information that tells you what happens in a story before you see it.
examples: Don’t read the reviews, they’re full of {spoilers}.
wrong: The spoiler kept the ending a complete secret.

words.meaning: A short film that shows parts of a new movie to advertise it.
examples: The {trailer} for the new film looks amazing.
wrong: The trailer is the full three-hour version of the movie.

words.meaning: A film or book that is very popular and makes a lot of money.
examples: The summer {blockbuster} broke box office records.
wrong: The blockbuster was seen by almost nobody.

words.meaning: A funny TV series about the same characters in everyday situations.
examples: My favorite {sitcom} is about a group of friends in a café.
wrong: The sitcom is a serious news program about politics.

words.meaning: A short performance to show if you are good enough for a part in a show.
examples: She sang a song at her {audition} for the musical.
wrong: He had an audition after the show had already finished its run.

words.meaning: An extra song or piece performed at the end because the audience asks for more.
examples: The crowd shouted for an {encore}, so the band played one more song.
wrong: The encore is the first song a band plays when it arrives.

words.meaning: A line of people, bands and decorated vehicles moving through the streets to celebrate.
examples: Thousands watched the {parade} on the main street.
wrong: The parade stood still in an empty room with no one watching.

words.meaning: A performance where one person stands on stage and tells jokes.
examples: He does {stand-up comedy} in small clubs.
wrong: Stand-up comedy is a sad song played on the violin.

words.meaning: A person who does magic tricks to entertain people.
examples: The {magician} pulled a rabbit out of a hat.
wrong: The magician cooked dinner in the hotel kitchen every night.

words.meaning: A traveling show with clowns, acrobats and sometimes animals, usually in a big tent.
examples: The {circus} is in town for one week.
wrong: The circus is a quiet room for studying.

words.meaning: Something you do regularly for fun in your free time.
examples: Fishing is his favorite {pastime}.
wrong: His pastime is the work he does every day to earn money.

words.meaning: Time when you are not working and can relax.
examples: Most people spend their {leisure} time with family.
wrong: She has no leisure because she does nothing but relax all week.

words.meaning: A performer whose job is to make people laugh by telling jokes.
examples: The {comedian} had the whole audience laughing.
wrong: The comedian made everyone cry with his sad, serious talk.

words.meaning: A group of people who sing together.
examples: She sings in the school {choir}.
wrong: The choir played drums without singing a note.

words.meaning: Small objects that explode with colored lights and loud noises in the sky.
examples: We watched the {fireworks} on New Year’s Eve.
wrong: The fireworks lit up the sky silently at noon.

words.meaning: An evening when you go out to enjoy yourself, for example at a restaurant or club.
examples: We’re planning a {night out} for her birthday.
wrong: Our night out was a quiet evening at home in bed.

words.meaning: To do something to make waiting pass more quickly.
examples: We played cards to {kill time} at the airport.
wrong: I killed time by working hard to finish before the deadline.

words.meaning: To like or be very interested in something.
examples: My brother {is into} jazz and plays the sax.
wrong: She’s into tennis, so she hates every match.
